message.content:
**Union Square Greenmarket** – the largest and most‑visited farmers’ market in New York City. | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Location** | 14th Street & Union Square, Manhattan | | **Hours** | Tuesday–Saturday: 8 a.m. – 2 p.m. (closed Sundays) | | **Annual Footfall** | Roughly **1.5 million visitors** per year (estimates from NYC Department of Cultural Affairs and market operators) | | **Why it’s the most visited** | • It’s the city’s flagship farmers’ market, drawing both locals and tourists.
• It offers a wide variety of fresh produce, artisanal foods, and seasonal specialties.
• Its central location and proximity to major transit hubs (Union Square subway station, several bus lines) make it highly accessible.
• The market hosts special events, cooking demos, and seasonal festivals that attract large crowds. | Other notable markets in NYC include: - **Chelsea Market** – a food hall and mixed‑use development in the Meatpacking District, popular for its diverse eateries and boutique shops. - **Grand Central Market** – a smaller, community‑focused market in the East Village. - **Brooklyn Flea** – a weekend flea market in Williamsburg, known for vintage goods and local crafts. However, when it comes to sheer visitor numbers and overall popularity, Union Square Greenmarket remains the top‑ranked market in New York City.
